source: «Lettere di Carlo De Franceschi a Giovanni Kobler», printed 1928, pp. 107–207 — a hundred pages of letters written between 6 February 1873 and 19 June 1889, most from Parenzo. The family holds a scan. It was read through in September 2026 and the passages below are all of it that touches the family, its parish and its name.

quotes.it: Quel Giovanni Batt. De Franceschi venuto dalla Contea di Pisino, come Ella dice, intorno al 1740 è senz'altro proveniente dalla mia famiglia.
quotes.en: That Giovanni Battista De Franceschi who came from the County of Pazin, as you say, around 1740, is without doubt from my family.
quotes.why: The single sentence this archive has been working toward. The man the received account treats as a separate line is claimed, by the family's own historian, as one of them.

quotes.it: Suo padre, mio trisavolo, pure Giambattista del fu Leonardo, ebbe due figli Giampietro e Giambattista.
quotes.en: His father, my great-great-grandfather, also a Giambattista, son of the late Leonardo, had two sons: Giampietro and Giambattista.
quotes.why: Three generations named. And «Giambattista del fu Leonardo» is exactly the phrase the Gologorica register uses in 1769 — «Joannes Baptista Defranceschi filius Leonardi» — the entry that gives the casa-31 branch its byname «detti Leonardi».

quotes.it: Anche i miei derivano dalla Carnia, ma si stabilirono in Istria intorno al 1700.
quotes.en: Mine too derive from Carnia, but they settled in Istria around 1700.
quotes.why: The Gologorica family says of itself that it came from Carnia. The 1679 headmen's list already put a De Franceschi of Mione in the County of Pazin; this is the other end of the same road, stated by a descendant.

quotes.it: Il mio trisavolo fabbricò la nostra casa nel 1711 come da relativa iscrizione.
quotes.en: My great-great-grandfather built our house in 1711, as the inscription on it says.
quotes.why: The house on the Gologorica square, dated 1711 — built by Giambattista del fu Leonardo. The inscription this archive hoped somebody would photograph was read by Carlo himself.

quotes.it: Ma ve n'ha tuttodì a Mione e Muina della Carnia.
quotes.en: But there are still some of them today at Mione and Muina in Carnia.
quotes.why: Mione, named by Carlo De Franceschi. Muina is the next village along the same valley — both frazioni of Ovaro.

quotes.it: I nostri in origine erano da Bergamo, poi venuti in Carnia, dove avevano castelli, poi fortemente decaduti si dispersero.
quotes.en: Ours were originally from Bergamo, then came into Carnia, where they had castles, then fell badly and scattered.
quotes.why: The family's own tradition of itself, as told to Carlo by a cousin, Corrado, from papers kept in that branch. Bergamo before Carnia — a claim this archive had no way to reach.

quotes.it: Noi abbiamo stemma: nella parte superiore dello scudo una croce greca attraversata da due freccie, nell'inferiore un melagrano; sovra lo scudo elmo piumato.
quotes.en: We have arms: in the upper part of the shield a Greek cross crossed by two arrows, in the lower a pomegranate; above the shield a plumed helm.
quotes.why: The arms of this family, blazoned by its own head. Every heraldry catalogue consulted for this archive offered something else entirely.

quotes.it: Il nostro nome originario è veramente De Franceschi… Ma venuti negli stati austriaci sembrò alle autorità che volessero arrogarsi il titolo di nobiltà, non sapendo questi che il «de» in Italia aggiunto al nome esprime il casato, e non titolo nobiliare, onde essi nei decreti scrivevano Defranceschi.
quotes.en: Our original name is truly De Franceschi… But once they had come into the Austrian states it seemed to the authorities that they meant to arrogate a title of nobility — those authorities not knowing that in Italy the «de» added to a name expresses the house, not a title — so in their decrees they wrote Defranceschi.
quotes.why: The fused spelling explained by a man it was done to. Some signed Defranceschi for fear of the fine for claiming nobility they could not prove; others kept De Franceschi; a few went to plain Franceschi.

pedigree: the eponym; his son is «Giambattista del fu Leonardo»
Carlo's great-great-grandfather. Built the Gologorica house in 1711. Two sons.
the elder; a fedecommesso was settled on him in the custom of the time

the younger; meant for the priesthood, studied at Fiume, «felt a vocation for the sword instead» and volunteered in Maria Theresa's army. Made castellan of Bribir for his service; married a lady of the D'Agnese family.
descendants: Chancellor of the County of Pazin in the last century
known to Carlo in 1848; employed at the Trieste customs house
moved to Zadar and went into the revenue service; the Zadar De Franceschi keep the names Giambattista and Vincenzo
port captain of Fiume — descended, Carlo thought, not from Giambattista but from Valentino, who came to Fiume directly from Carnia, and who told Carlo his ancestors came from there
a De Franceschi drawing master and perhaps engineer at the Fiume gymnasium when Carlo studied there, 1820–1826

correction.heading: And then, two months later, Carlo corrected himself
correction.lead: The pedigree above comes from the letter of 10 November 1876. On 31 January 1877 Carlo wrote again, having had more from Kobler, and withdrew part of it — which this archive had been repeating as his conclusion.
correction.quote: Adesso, la di Lei mercè, sono in chiaro riguardo al ramo della mia famiglia stabilitasi a Fiume. Io confondeva il primo Giambattista col secondo di lui figlio, di nome pure Giovanni, ritenendo che già quello era a Bribir. E mi rincresce assai di non aver saputo che il vivente Francesco sia mio terzo cugino.
correction.en: Now, thanks to you, I am clear about the branch of my family settled at Fiume. I was confusing the first Giambattista with his son, also called Giovanni, believing that the first was already at Bribir. And I am very sorry not to have known that the living Francesco is my third cousin.
correction.why: So Francesco, harbour-master of Fiume, is not descended from a Valentino who came from Carnia in 1739. He is Carlo's own third cousin, four generations down from the same Giambattista del fu Leonardo. Carlo had spent five years living in Fiume knowing the man only slightly, and says so with real regret: «avrei fatto con esso Francesco relazione ben più stretta» — I would have made a far closer connection with him.

trees.note: Carlo drew the two lines side by side in the letter. They are printed as two columns and this is how they read.

gologorica.heading: What his family actually did at Gologorica
gologorica.lead: The single most useful thing in the correspondence, and it is buried in a technical exchange about the Urbaria of the County of Pisino, dated 19 March 1877.
gologorica.quote: Negli Urbari non compariscono Gollogorizza, Tupliaco e Scopliaco, perchè ne era Dominus il vescovo di Pedena. A questi Gollogorizza pagava non già la decima, ma un invariabile annuo corrispettivo in vino, frumento, avena, agnelli, galline ed uova, locchè chiamavasi «affitto fermo», forse per seguito antico accordo. Questo affitto fermo sino alla soppressione del vescovato veniva percepito dalla mia famiglia a titolo di affittanza, rinnovata da ogni vescovo, a cui pagava il convenuto importo. Prima che Gollogorizza fosse dei vescovi di Pedena, era un bene della nobile famiglia Schnal di Pisino.
gologorica.en: Gologorica, Tupljak and Škopljak do not appear in the Urbaria, because the bishop of Pedena was their Lord. To him Gologorica paid not a tithe but a fixed annual render in wine, wheat, oats, lambs, hens and eggs, which was called the «affitto fermo» — the firm rent — perhaps following some ancient agreement. Until the suppression of the bishopric this firm rent was collected by my family as lessees, the lease renewed by every bishop, to whom we paid the agreed sum. Before Gologorica belonged to the bishops of Pedena it was a holding of the noble Schnal family of Pisino.
gologorica.why: This is what the De Franceschi were at Gologorica. Not landowners and not peasants — the men who farmed the bishop's rent, holding a lease renewed at every episcopal succession, collecting wine, grain, oats, lambs, hens and eggs from their neighbours and paying the bishop a fixed sum. It is a middleman's position, and a durable one: it ran until the diocese of Pedena was suppressed in 1788. It also explains why the bishops styled themselves «Dominus Gollaegoritiae» and why a village of a few dozen houses turns up in a bishop's title at all — a point Carlo also makes, from the other end, in his book.

bells.heading: He began his collection of Istrian bell inscriptions with his own village
bells.lead: From the letter of 10 November 1876, written at Gologorica — «mio luogo natale», my birthplace — where he had gone to spend a whole month with his family after a bereavement.

rows.text: «Una porta in caratteri gotici rotondi l'epigrafe 1364: Magister Nicholaus me fecit.» One carries, in round gothic letters, the date 1364 and the words Master Nicholaus made me. «Ella vede che è ben vecchia» — you see it is very old indeed. A second bell by the same Nicolò and his brother Giovanni, a few years later, hangs at Zarečje.

Three inscriptions on one bell. In square gothic: «A fulgure et tempestate libera nos Domine» — from lightning and tempest deliver us, O Lord. In round gothic: «Facta sub Plebano Georgio Challigarich opus Ioannis Albinus 1573» — made under the parish priest Juraj Kaligarić, the work of Ivan Albinus. And beneath those, four Glagolitic letters, which Carlo sent to Volčić to interpret and never reports an answer for.

bells.close: Carlo's plan was to collect the bell inscriptions of the whole of Istria. He started with the bells he had grown up under.

bribir.heading: The siege of Bribir
bribir.lead: Giambattista, the brother meant for the priesthood, was made castellan of Bribir after the Seven Years' War. Carlo tells what happened there as a story he had from his elders.
bribir.text: «È interessante il racconto della sua difesa con pochi servi contro una feroce banda di masnadieri forte di 40 e più uomini, che assaltarono e presero finalmente il castello, dopo che egli dall'ultimo suo servo rimasto vivo fu calato nel fondo d'una torre, dove i ladroni nol poterono trovare.» — The account of his defence, with a few servants, against a fierce band of brigands forty and more strong, who attacked and at last took the castle, after his last surviving servant had lowered him into the bottom of a tower where the robbers could not find him.
bribir.coda: And then the other half of it, which is why the story survived: «Il vecchio mio professore Potosniak mi narrava d'aver dato gli estremi sacramenti al terribile condottiero di quella banda, morto assai vecchio, e che gli espose la lunghissima serie di tutti i suoi misfatti.» — My old teacher Potočnjak told me he had given the last rites to the terrible leader of that band, dead very old, who laid out for him the very long series of all his crimes. A branch of the family lived at Bribir until about 1836, then moved to Zadar.

razvod.heading: A scholar's opinion worth recording
razvod.text: Twice in these letters Carlo states, flatly, that the Istrian Razvod — the famous boundary act dated 1325, one of the oldest documents in the Croatian language and a monument of Glagolitic writing — is not genuine: «Gli studii che ho fatto sul famoso Razvod istriano del 1325 mi inducono a ritenerlo un'impostura elaborata intorno al 1500 nel castello di Pisino.» An imposture put together around 1500 in Pisino castle. Kobler held it authentic, and Carlo notes the disagreement politely — «che io per motivi a Lei noti ammetto come genuino» he writes of Kobler's position, not his own.
razvod.why: It has no bearing on the family. It is here because it shows what kind of reader Carlo was, and because it is the strongest opinion he expresses anywhere in a hundred pages of otherwise mild correspondence.

otherhalf.heading: And now the other half of it
otherhalf.lead: Everything above is Carlo writing to Kobler, from the 1928 printing. Kobler's own letters — the questions Carlo was answering — were edited by Jakov Jelinčić and published in three parts in the Vjesnik of the Rijeka and Pazin archives in 1977, 1978 and after. They are open access, and this archive did not know they existed until September 2026.
otherhalf.never: Jelinčić opens with a fact worth sitting with. Kobler corresponded with De Franceschi for sixteen years — and «čini se da se Kobler i de Franceschi usprkos obostranoj želji nikada nisu osobno upoznali»: it seems that Kobler and de Franceschi, despite wanting to on both sides, never met in person.

question.heading: The question that produced the famous answer
question.text: Kobler had gone through the civic records of Fiume and listed every Defranceschi household he could find there. Then he sent the list to Carlo and asked, in four words: «È forse Lei un Discendente?» — Are you perhaps a descendant? Carlo's reply is the letter this archive has built half its Carnia argument on.

valentino.heading: And Kobler's second entry is a document, not a tradition
valentino.text: «Valentino Defranceschi, venuto dalla Carnia, fu fatto Cittadino nel 1739, e colla moglie Elena ebbe 10 figli e 4 figlie, aveva casa in contrada dei Capuccini e vigna in Plase, fabbricò nel 1764 la Capella di S. Elena, fece per se tomba nel Duomo con epigrafe nel 1785 e morì nel 1785.»
valentino.en: Valentino Defranceschi, come from Carnia, was made a Citizen in 1739; by his wife Elena he had ten sons and four daughters; he had a house in the Capuchins' quarter and a vineyard at Plase; in 1764 he built the Chapel of St Helen; in 1785 he made himself a tomb in the Duomo with an epigraph; and he died in 1785. His son Ignazio married Giuseppa Danezello, was a Civic Representative in 1783, and died in 1785 aged forty.
valentino.why: This matters more than anything Carlo says about his own ancestors. The Carnia page of this archive has been resting on a single document — the headmen's list of 1679. Here is a second, from a different researcher working a different record set: Kobler, reading the civic registers of Fiume, states as a matter of record that a Defranceschi came from Carnia and was made a citizen in 1739. It does not connect anybody to this family. It does mean that Carnians of this surname demonstrably moved into the Kvarner in the eighteenth century, which is the whole mechanism the family's own tradition describes.
valentino.then: And Valentino left two things that can still be looked for: the Chapel of St Helen at Rijeka, built 1764, and his tomb in the cathedral with an epigraph of 1785.

otherhalf.source: Jakov Jelinčić, «Korespondencija Giovanni Kobler — Carlo De Franceschi», Vjesnik historijskih arhiva u Rijeci i Pazinu XXI (1977) pp. 181–196, XXII (1978) pp. 37–57, and part III. Open access on Hrčak.

obituary.heading: How the Istrian press buried him, January 1893
obituary.lead: «Il giovine Pensiero» of Pola for 25 January 1893 runs a piece on three men the Italian movement had lost in a few months, and it names them together: Carlo Dordi of Trento, Carlo Favetti of Gorizia, and Carlo De Franceschi of Istria. «E chi sono dessi?» — and who are they?
obituary.quote: Il terzo è l'illustre istriano Carlo de Franceschi, che venne a mancare il giorno otto di questo mese. Non meno dei primi, sì per ingegno che per patriotismo, passò tutta la sua vita piena di sacrifici ed abnegazione studiando e combattendo per difendere l'italianità dell'Istria…
obituary.en: The third is the illustrious Istrian Carlo de Franceschi, who died on the eighth of this month. No less than the first two, in talent as in patriotism, he passed his whole life full of sacrifices and self-denial, studying and fighting to defend the Italianness of Istria.
obituary.grave: And then the line this archive had been looking for without knowing it: «l'illustre storiografo riposa nell'umile cimitero» — the illustrious historian rests in the humble cemetery of his own village. Box 12 of the family archive in Zagreb holds the architect Giuseppe Hirsch's printed plan for the «Cappella della famiglia di Carlo de Franceschi nel cimitero di Moncalvo di Pisino». The chapel and the grave are the same story, and neither has been photographed.

funeral.heading: The week of the funeral: three notices, January 1893
funeral.lead: Carlo De Franceschi died at Gologorica on 8 January 1893. Within ten days the Istrian Italian press had printed a career obituary, a front-page life, and a letter from Pisino by a man who had sat with him. All three were found in the Austrian National Library's newspaper archive (ANNO) in September 2026 and read through the page images. None of them had been in this archive before.
funeral.caution: How these were read. The scans were located by OCR — the engine here has no Italian model — and then every passage quoted below was enlarged on the page image and read letter by letter against the type. What is inside quotation marks is what the paper printed, including its own compositor's slips, which are marked. Sentences summarised rather than quoted are marked as summaries.

items.kicker: The career, and why it stopped
items.text: A full column, opening «Un'altra nobile figura di patriota, di scienziato e di storico, è sparita» — another noble figure of patriot, scientist and historian has vanished. It runs the career: Fiume for gymnasium, Gorizia for philosophy, Graz for law; a trainee at the Rovigno tribunal from 1832, rising to assessor; elected in 1848 to represent Pisino, Rovigno and Dignano at the Vienna parliament and then at Kremsier.
items.quote: ma nell'anno 1854, nel nuovo ordinamento amministrativo, venne cassato dal ruolo degli impiegati e messo in quiescenza per sospetti politici.
items.en: but in the year 1854, under the new administrative order, he was struck off the roll of officials and pensioned off on suspicion of political sympathies.
items.why: This archive already knew Carlo lost his post in 1854. It did not have the reason in print. The paper goes on to say the pension left him so little that he had to leave for Fiume «onde provvedere al mantenimento della propria famiglia» — to provide for the keep of his own family — where he found a place in the office of the advocate Thierry and stayed until 1861, when the Istrian Provincial Committee made him its secretary. The figure the paper gives for the reduced pension is damaged on the scan and is not repeated here.

items.kicker: What was still in his desk
items.text: The obituary closes by listing what he left unpublished — and it is the plainest statement this archive has of what was in the house at Gologorica on the day he died.
items.why: The memoirs did reach print, but not for thirty-three years: his son Camillo published them at Trieste in 1926. In January 1893 they were a manuscript in a house at Gologorica that nobody outside the family had read. Boxes 1 to 5 of the family archive now in Zagreb are described in the published inventory as Carlo's own working papers, which is where the unfinished study on the nationality of Istria should be looked for first.
items.quote: A tanta attività d'ingegno egli lascia morendo un volume di memorie ed uno studio incompleto sulla nazionalità dell'Istria, ed altri lavori d'indole minore, e che speriamo — massime i primi due — di vederli presto per le stampe, essendo quei documenti troppo importanti per noi e per i tempi che corrono.
items.en: To so much activity of mind he leaves, dying, a volume of memoirs and an unfinished study on the nationality of Istria, and other works of lesser kind — and we hope, above all for the first two, to see them soon in print, those documents being too important for us and for the times we are living through.

items.kicker: A birth date the reference books do not give
items.quote: L'illustre storiografo e scienziato Carlo De Franceschi nacque a Moncalvo (Gollogorizza) il 17 Ottobre 1810 da famiglia abbastanza agiata.
items.en: The illustrious historian and scientist Carlo De Franceschi was born at Moncalvo (Gologorica) on 17 October 1810, of a reasonably comfortable family.
items.why: Two things. First, the standard reference date for Carlo's birth is 16 October 1809; both papers printed within ten days of his death give 17 October, and this one gives 1810. That is not a correction — a newspaper is not a baptismal register, and the Gologorica register is the only thing that will settle it — but it is a discrepancy this archive should carry openly rather than quietly adopt the tidier date. Second, and worth more: «da famiglia abbastanza agiata». It is the only contemporary description this archive holds of the standing of the Gologorica household in the generation before Carlo — comfortable, not poor, not noble.

items.cite: «Il giovine Pensiero», same issue, «Corrispondenze istriane»: Pisino, 15 January 1893, signed «Don Ramiro»
items.kicker: The man, from six days after the burial
items.text: A letter from Pisino, and the only piece of the three written by somebody describing his own habits. He will not hear him again in his favourite seat at the Casino di Società; he will not see «brillare i suoi occhi di fuoco giovanile» — his eyes flash with youthful fire — when he spoke of the national struggles.
items.quote: Non lo si vedrà più nella giornata di sabato in piazza della fontana, attorniato dai poveri del Comune, spargere largamente l'elemosima [sic], intrattenendosi a lungo ed affabilmente seco loro. Il nostro amatissimo Sor Carlo riposa ora in pace nell'umile cimitero di Moncalvo.
items.en: He will no longer be seen on a Saturday in the fountain square, surrounded by the poor of the commune, handing out alms freely and staying a long while talking with them affably. Our much-loved Sor Carlo now rests in peace in the humble cemetery of Moncalvo.
items.why: «Sor Carlo», in italics in the paper — the Istrian familiar, not «l'illustre storiografo». And a fixed weekly habit in the square at Pisino, remembered by name six days after the burial. The cemetery line is the same one this archive found in the paper's issue of 25 January, printed a week earlier and by somebody who had stood there. The misprint «elemosima» for «elemosina» is the compositor's and is kept as set.

items.cite: «Il giovine Pensiero», same issue, review column
items.kicker: And a scholarly position, confirmed in public
items.text: The same issue reviews Carlo's study of the Chersano document — the copy of the Istrian Razvod found, corroded, among the old papers of Momiano castle, with two further copies that Tomaso Luciani of Albona dug out of the Venetian archives at Carlo's request. The paper reports his verdict: the document is «apocrifo e falsato in lingua slava fra il 1400-1500», forged into Slavic between 1400 and 1500, most likely at the instance of a count of Pisino.
items.why: In the Kobler letters Carlo says the same thing privately, and this archive already records it. This is the first time we can show he had said it in public, and that the Istrian press was still arguing about it in the week he was buried.

funeral.croatian: One more search, and it did not stay a blank. This archive went looking for the other side of the argument — «Naša Sloga», the Croatian paper of Istria, which fought the De Franceschi of Gologorica in print for forty years. Two issues name them. The first, 13 April 1900, is a false lead: «Načelnikom u Umagu bijaše izabran dne 9. t. mj. g. Fr. de Franceschi, bivši načelnik one općine» — a Fr. de Franceschi elected mayor of Umag, ninety kilometres west, and nothing yet connects him. The second, 25 March 1909, is the thing itself: the paper takes page 351 of Carlo's own «L'Istria», with its 1102 charter and its three Slavic place-names, and turns his argument inside out. It is set out on the Gologorica line, because it is about the village rather than about him.
funeral.close: Reading order, for what it is worth: «L'Eco di Pola» tells you what he did, «Il giovine Pensiero» tells you where he came from, and Don Ramiro's letter from Pisino tells you what it was like to stand next to him on a Saturday morning.

chapel.heading: Valentino's chapel, and the words over its door
chapel.lead: This archive has been carrying Kobler's one-sentence summary of Valentino Defranceschi for months — came from Carnia, made a citizen in 1739, built the chapel of St Helen in 1764, made himself a tomb, died in 1785 — and noting that the chapel and the tomb were things that could still be looked for. Kobler's «Memorie per la storia della città di Fiume» were reprinted whole in the «Atti» of Rovigno in 1978, and they are free on the Internet Archive. The full entry is four times as long, and it gives the inscription.
chapel.quote: 25. La Cappella di S. Elena. — Esiste presso il confine occidentale, poco più in là di S. Giovanni. Sulla porta d'ingresso si legge incisa l'epigrafe: «Sacellum B. Mariæ Virgini erectum a D. Valentino Defranceschi a. 1764». Quel Defranceschi era venuto a Fiume dalla Carnia circa l'anno 1730, aveva una moglie di nome Elena, e possedeva una casa in Fiume e una vigna in Plasse. Morì nel 1785, e fu sepolto nel Duomo.
chapel.en: 25. The Chapel of St Helen. — It stands near the western boundary, a little beyond San Giovanni. Over the entrance door is cut the inscription: «A chapel raised to the Blessed Virgin Mary by Signor Valentino Defranceschi in the year 1764». That Defranceschi had come to Fiume from Carnia about the year 1730; he had a wife named Elena, and owned a house in Fiume and a vineyard at Plase. He died in 1785 and was buried in the Duomo.

rows.lab: The name is cut in stone, and Kobler read it there
rows.text: «Sacellum B. Mariæ Virgini erectum a D. Valentino Defranceschi a. 1764.» Not a register entry, not a tradition, not a citation — a lintel. And the D. is Dominus, the same title the Gologorica registers give a Josephus Defranceschi in the same decades and the same title the Rovigno scholarship says a Carnian earned in Istria by buying land.

rows.lab: It is called St Helen's and his wife was Elena
rows.text: Kobler puts the two facts in consecutive clauses without joining them: the chapel is dedicated by its inscription to the Blessed Virgin, it is known as the chapel of St Helen, and «aveva una moglie di nome Elena». A man building a chapel and letting it be called by his wife's name-saint is not proof of anything. It is also not nothing.

«era venuto a Fiume dalla Carnia circa l'anno 1730» — he came to Fiume from Carnia about 1730, and was made a citizen in 1739. Nine years from arrival to citizenship. Carlo, writing privately a century and a half later, said his family came over from Carnia around 1700; the 1679 headmen's list has a Zuane De Franceschi of Mione already working in the County of Pazin. Valentino is a later crossing on the same road, and the only one with a year on it.

rows.lab: And it stood there in Kobler's own time
rows.text: «Esiste presso il confine occidentale, poco più in là di S. Giovanni» — it exists, in the present tense, near the western boundary a little beyond San Giovanni: Sveti Ivan, on the western side of Rijeka, near Plase where his vineyard was. Kobler was writing in the 1890s. Whether it is standing now, nobody in this archive has looked.

rows.lab: What happened to it after him
rows.text: The care of the chapel passed in 1801 to the Faribault family, who had bought the vineyard; and in 1839 Celestino Faribault gave a guarantee for its upkeep and for fourteen masses a year. So it was maintained, under an endowment, for at least seventy-five years after Valentino's death, by people who had bought his land.

chapel.tomb: And the tomb is confirmed from the same volume. In his account of the collegiate church, Kobler lists the burials that still had their slabs: after the chapter's own vault and the tomb of Bishop Giovanni Antonio de Benzoni, the family tombs of the Stemberg, Velens, Saurich, Troyer, Lumaga and the rest, and then the individual stones — «Giorgio Marchesetti, Valentino Defranceschi, Francesco Calucci…». He adds that almost all of them are eighteenth-century, because the great restoration of 1716–1726 took up the slabs of the extinct families. Valentino's was still in the floor when Kobler walked over it.
chapel.todo: Two things to ask for, and they are the most photographable leads this archive has. First, whether the chapel of St Helena above Sveti Ivan still stands, and whether the 1764 lintel is still on it. Second, whether the floor slab is still in the church at Rijeka. Both are questions for the Rijeka conservation office or the parish, and neither needs an archive appointment.
chapel.source: Giovanni Kobler, «Memorie per la storia della liburnica città di Fiume», reprinted complete as vol. 3 of the Collana degli Atti of the Centro di ricerche storiche di Rovigno, 1978 — read from the Internet Archive copy, September 2026. The chapel is no. 25 in his list of the chapels of Fiume; the tombs are in his chapter on the collegiate church.

threestocks.heading: Kobler's own article on the family, which this archive had never read
threestocks.lead: The «Memorie» close with a long dictionary of the families of Fiume, house by house and marriage by marriage, out of the civic registers. It has an entry headed «De Franceschi e Defranceschi», and it opens by refusing to do what a family history usually does.
threestocks.open: «In Fiume vi furono tre stirpi dei Franceschi; ma non è constatato, se abbiano avuto uno stipite comune. La stirpe più antica si trova registrata De Franceschi, le altre due Defranceschi.» — In Fiume there were three stocks of the Franceschi, but it is not established whether they had a common ancestor. The oldest is registered De Franceschi, the other two Defranceschi. Kobler was Carlo De Franceschi's correspondent and friend, and he still would not join them up.

stocks.t: Stirpe De Franceschi — the old Fiume house
rows: «un Domenico di Francesco si univa in matrimonio con Lucia Trassich» — Domenico di Francesco marries Lucia Trassich. Their children are entered sometimes De Franceschi, sometimes de Francesco; the surname is still forming.

Two of those sons are municipal councillors. Giovanni Paolo, who in 1654 married Margherita, widow of Michele Androcha, had a house by St Vitus and died in 1684. Marco Antonio, who in 1664 married Francesca di Piergiovanni and had sons Giovanni and Marzio.

Giovanni Antonio, son of Giovanni Paolo: doctor of laws, municipal councillor, and civic chancellor of Fiume from 1694. «Egli si firmava De Franceschi» — he signed himself De Franceschi. He died in 1727 «e fu l'ultimo maschio di questa famiglia in Fiume», the last male of this family in Fiume: no sons of his own, and his brother's sons moved away.
And then the sentence

«Ora una famiglia De Franceschi si trova in Istria con possessioni in Golagorica.» — Now a De Franceschi family is found in Istria with possessions at Gologorica. That is how Kobler ends the article on the oldest Fiume stock: by pointing at this family's village.

stocks.t: I Defranceschi del Friuli — Valentino's house
rows: «Valentino, che accennasi venuto dalla Carnia, trovasi in Fiume circa l'anno 1730.» By his wife Elena, between 1737 and 1759, ten sons and four daughters. Made a citizen in 1739.
The property

A house in the Capuchins' quarter, and «vigna con casa in Plasse sul confine di Castua» — a vineyard with a house at Plase on the Kastav boundary. There, Kobler says here, he had the chapel of St Helena built in 1761, its front carrying «Sacellum a D. Valentino Defranceschi erectum a. 1764».
The tomb, word for word

He died aged eighty-five and was buried in the collegiate church by the altar of the Madonna del Carmine, under a stone reading «Cineres D. Valentini De Franceschi, qui vivens sibi ac posteris suis destinavit hanc aeternae quietis sedem» — the ashes of Dominus Valentinus De Franceschi, who while he lived appointed this seat of eternal rest for himself and for his descendants.
His son

«Suo figlio Ignazio nel 1775 prese in moglie Giuseppa Donegalli, fu rappresentante civico nell'anno 1783, e morì nel 1785 di anni 40.» Ignazio married Giuseppa Donegalli in 1775, was a civic representative in 1783, and died in 1785 aged forty — the same year as his father.
And the rest
«Dove passassero gli altri, non si sa.» Where the others went is not known. Fourteen children, and Kobler can follow one.

stocks.t: La presente famiglia Defranceschi — the house from Pisino
rows: «Giovanni Battista, venuto da Pisino dell'Istria, abitava in Fiume circa l'anno 1740, e fu fatto cittadino nel 1746.» Giovanni Battista, come from Pisino in Istria, living at Fiume about 1740 and made a citizen in 1746. Sons: Giuseppe, Vincenzo and Giovanni.
Giuseppe, 1748–1778
Married Francesca Tomasich in 1772, died in 1778 leaving a son Valentino; the widow remarried in 1783 to Giovanni Bassan.
Valentino di Giuseppe

Civic engineer and steward of Fiume, with a house on the Corso until 1827. Married Orsola de Benzoni in 1793; sons Francesco Giuseppe, Giovanni Nepomuceno, Pietro Giulio and Antonio, daughters Teresa, Lodovica, Giuseppa and Anna. His wife died in 1807 and he built a family tomb in the cemetery where she lay.
Francesco Giuseppe
Patrician councillor and royal harbourmaster of Fiume. Died 22 December 1885 — within Carlo's lifetime, and within Kobler's.
And the third son

«Giovanni, terzo figlio di Giovanni Battista, era castellano di Bribir nel Vinodol, ove morì nel 1807.» Giovanni, third son of Giovanni Battista, was castellan of Bribir in the Vinodol, where he died in 1807. He owned a small house in Fiume in the St Barbara quarter, between the Zanchi and Mauro houses. A Lodovico, clerk of the civic magistrate in 1814, may have been his son.

collision.heading: And the third stock walks straight into Carlo's own story
collision.text: Read stock III beside what Carlo told Kobler in his letters, which is on this page above. Carlo's great-great-grandfather Giambattista del fu Leonardo built the Gologorica house in 1711 and had two sons; the younger, Giovanni Battista, was meant for the priesthood, «studied at Fiume», felt a vocation for the sword instead, volunteered in Maria Theresa's army, and was made castellan of Bribir. A branch of the family lived at Bribir until about 1836 and then moved to Zadar.
collision.then: Kobler, working from the civic registers of Fiume and not from Carlo, has a Giovanni Battista who came from Pisino about 1740 and was made a citizen in 1746 — and a castellan of Bribir in the family. The two accounts differ on which generation held the castle: Carlo makes it Giovanni Battista himself, Kobler makes it Giovanni, his third son, dead there in 1807. Gologorica is fifteen kilometres from Pisino, and «da Pisino» in a Fiume register means the district, not the town.
collision.why: This is the closest the archive has come to joining the Gologorica family to a Fiume household by documents rather than by tradition. It is not joined. Kobler himself declined to join his three stocks to one another, and he had both the registers and Carlo's letters in front of him. But two independent tellings — a family's own memory and a city's civic rolls — put a Giovanni Battista of the Pisino country in Fiume in the 1740s and a castellan of Bribir in the same house, and that is a coincidence worth naming out loud.

threestocks.discrepancies: Three places where the reprint disagrees with what this archive already published from Kobler, all of them small and all of them Kobler's own. He gives the chapel as built in 1761 in the family article and dated 1764 by its inscription, and he transcribes the inscription twice with different wording — «Sacellum B. Mariæ Virgini erectum a D. Valentino Defranceschi a. 1764» in the chapter on the chapels, and «Sacellum a D. Valentino Defranceschi erectum a. 1764» in the family article. And Ignazio's wife is «Giuseppa Donegalli» here, where this archive had «Giuseppa Danezello» from the earlier reading. The stone, if it survives, settles the first two; the marriage register at Rijeka settles the third.
threestocks.source_stocks: Giovanni Kobler, «Memorie per la storia della liburnica città di Fiume», reprinted as vol. 3 of the Collana degli Atti of Rovigno, 1978, pp. 157–159 in the reprint's pagination — read from the Internet Archive copy, September 2026.
